reflections.title: A country makes the four-day work week law
reflections.statement: Parliament passes a law that cuts the standard work week from five days to four, with no cut in pay. Employers get two years to adjust, and overtime will start after 32 hours. Hospitals, shops and factories that must stay open will need new shift patterns.

reflections.title: A child takes a toy back from a friend's hand
reflections.statement: One child pulls a toy out of a friend's hand and will not let the friend play with it. The Subject is this single moment: the grabbing, the refusal to share, and what it means for the two children and the toy between them. It is not a judgment of the child, only the act and what it sets in motion.

reflections.title: A lion hunts a deer: the chase, the kill, the meal
reflections.statement: A lion crouches in tall grass, picks out one deer and breaks cover. The deer runs, twisting and turning, and the lion closes in. He brings her down, kills her and eats.

reflections.title: A country takes in a large, sudden wave of refugees
reflections.statement: A war next door sends hundreds of thousands of people across the border within a few months. The host country must decide how to receive them, and its economy, identity, institutions and everyday trust between people are all touched at once.

reflections.title: How can Western civilization safeguard itself against rising rival powers?
reflections.statement: Western civilization grew into a place where freedom, prosperity and human rights are protected. Rival powers with other values are now strong enough to challenge the world order it built. The question is how, if at all, it should act to preserve what it is.

reflections.title: Humanity under one government instead of many nations
reflections.statement: Today humanity is divided into about two hundred countries, each with its own borders, laws and armies. The idea is that people could one day be governed by a single entity, and countries as we know them would end. This Reflection considers that idea as a whole, not any one route to it.

reflections.title: A town replaces its weekly street market with a permanent covered hall
reflections.statement: For forty years the market filled the high street every Saturday and was packed away by evening. The council has voted to build a covered hall with fixed stalls, open six days a week. The street will be returned to traffic.
